key_insight: Relit-LiVE jointly learns an environment-video representation together with a diffusion-based neural renderer, avoiding brittle intrinsic decomposition and producing photoreal, temporally consistent relit videos from real-world footage.
problem_solved: Existing relighting pipelines rely on accurate intrinsic decomposition (albedo, normals, etc.), which is unreliable on real videos and causes distorted appearance, broken materials, and temporal artifacts during relighting.
method: Jointly learn an explicit environment-video (time-varying illumination) representation and a diffusion-based neural renderer end-to-end, replacing separate intrinsic decomposition steps.
Condition a large-scale video diffusion model on the learned environment video and target illumination to render frames under novel lighting while preserving material appearance.
Enforce temporal consistency and material fidelity via temporal/perceptual constraints during training, producing stable, artifact-free relighting on real footage.
impact: Makes high-quality relighting of real-world videos practical without accurate intrinsic decomposition, benefiting VFX, AR/VR, dataset generation, and any application requiring realistic lighting edits or domain adaptation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input video → learn environment-video + diffusion renderer → relit output (show joint-learning loop)
Before/after frame pairs highlighting corrected materials and reduced artifacts
Environment-video visualization (sequence of HDR environment maps or light probes) to show learned illumination over time
Metric/time-series chart showing improved temporal consistency and perceptual scores versus decomposition-based baselines
paper_title: Relit-LiVE: Relight Video by Jointly Learning Environment Video
paper_authors: Weiqing Xiao, Hong Li, Xiuyu Yang, Houyuan Chen, Wenyi Li
